title: 2D image to hollowed 3D clothing? didn’t see that coming🫨
author: Proper-Flamingo-1783
selftext: not my work, but saw this post from Hirokazu Yokohara and had to share. All generated by Rodin Gen-2, honestly kind of insane how detailed the mesh is, even the inside of the clothing is actually hollowed out, not just flat geometry.  Anyone else tried using it? curious how it worked out for you.

comments.author: pierukainen
comments.body: I thought gen-2 is not out yet?

replies.author: Proper-Flamingo-1783
replies.body: They’ve opened an early access. Just replied to their X post and got a spot

replies.author: pierukainen
replies.body:
Lucky! Thanks for posting.

Do you have any initial impressions about how good it is for gamedev stuff?

comments.author: stepachess
comments.body: I don't know about this version but I tried 1.5 and a lot of other model generators. Yes clothes are strongest part of 3D AI but overall quality is not there still. If this new generator is easy you can try using it as guidelines in marvelous but from my experience they only showed best results and not what we will get on average.

replies.author: FesseJerguson
replies.body: I agree tried a bunch feels like we're close though!

comments.author: Still_Ad9431
comments.body: Rodin is worse than Trip, but it's better than Meshy

replies.author: spiffco7
replies.body: is this trip called tripo or is there another trip besides tripo3d.ai?

replies.author: _DDark_
replies.body: Is tripo meshes usable for games. Last I saw 3d ai gen dumps out a billion poly meshes or unusable garbage with holes.

replies.author: kid_dynamo
replies.body: Best case these things are a starting point for your High Poly. Especially for anything that needs to deform you will still need to do a lowpoly retopo. Cutting out the sculpting stage does save a ton of time though

replies.author: superkickstart
replies.body: None of the current mesh generators are. You still need tons of work to make them usable.

replies.author: TruWaves
replies.body: Just close the holes and do a quick retopo.

replies.author: justifun
replies.body: I find hitem3d the best so far but it doesn't do textures.

replies.author: AdFinal7385
replies.body: Rodin Gen-2 seems to be better. The current Gen-1.5 version performs well in sharp edges and hard surfaces, and it's watertight.

comments.author: DigitalDokkaebi
comments.body: Looks nice. If its hollow, how does it texture the inside?

comments.author: AxiosXiphos
comments.body: These are impressive but I assume these are the best results not the average?

replies.author: Proper-Flamingo-1783
replies.body: Just saw this by Hirokazu Yokohara on X. Maybe u can check their official account Deemos for more tutorials?

replies.author: Proper-Flamingo-1783
replies.body: Just head to hyper 3d.ai website. If u wanna try Gen-2, u can reply to their X post for early access

comments.author: Voltasoyle
comments.body: Now it just needs to be rigged, optimised, and given weights, and adjusted to prevent clipping, and yea, like 90% of the job remains.

replies.author: nightfend
replies.body: Or even just the back and sides

comments.author: nightfend
comments.body: The green jacket arms are welded into the main body. You could not rig that. Might be easier to just use it as inspiration and just remodel manually.

comments.author: Brilliant_Cry_4465
comments.body:
Another problem with these systems is there's no clear way to make the proportions match an existing character model

So you've got some clothes - now you have to clean out the inside of the mesh, likely clean up the topology and weights and looping, and it doesn't fit your character model anyway

I wish this stuff worked i'd use it all day
